Definition: apparently a primary word; twaddle, i.e. an incredible story:--idle tale.
BiblicalUsage: lēros means idle tale, and its few appearances are all worth reading. In Luke 24:11, "And their words seemed to them as idle tales".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the women's words seemed like idle tales because resurrection always sounds impossible until you see the empty tomb.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
